svg.title: TOPAK B5 — Promotion is a quorum grant, run as a round, and a promotion seats
svg.desc: ADR-0024 replaces the single promotion signing key, the last privileged human grant. Everything that crosses from Build to Run (boundary B1) is promoted by a round keyed by artifact digest: gates enable voting, grant seats vote, veto seats can only deny, the author is recused, and the tally reads its quorum from the issued rules. Since Batch 34 a promotion seats (ADR-0024 A3, provisional with ADR-0050): when the tally on a seating completes, the mechanism grants the principal's first lease. That is not built at the reference, where an unsigned BOOTSTRAP socket seats instead.
svg.text: TOPAK · B5

text.tspan: Promotion is a quorum grant, run as a round, and a promotion seats

svg.text: ADR-0024 replaces the single promotion signing key, the last privileged human grant. Everything that crosses from Build to Run (boundary B1) is promoted by a round keyed by artifact digest: gates enable voting, grant seats vote, veto seats can only deny, the author is recused, and the tally reads its quorum from the issued rules. Since Batch 34 a promotion seats (ADR-0024 A3, provisional with ADR-0050): when the tally on a
seating completes, the mechanism grants the principal's first lease. That is not built at the reference, where an unsigned BOOTSTRAP socket seats instead.

text.tspan: Issued rules at rules epoch e (anchor issuance, ADR-0025 §1 (a))

svg.text: The promotion roster and its parameters: grantSeats, vetoSeats, quorum ("all" or a threshold k) and minGrant, bounded by the rules floor (R1 unanimity, R2 minGrant ≥ 2, R5 no anchor key on the roster, R9 quorum = "all" ∨ quorum ≥ 2). This quorum cannot change its own rules (§2).
Drafts the artifact in its round workspace.
Ends with Submit(digest), or abstains with
Submit of ⊥ (ADR-0022 §1).
Holds no seat for its own artifact.

text.tspan: Gates enable voting; they do not vote

svg.text: ADR-0007 totality, non-vacuity and discrimination
gates.
bundle ⊑ floor (ADR-0010; listed in §4). By
ADR-0030 composition it holds for every bundle, so
ToO §7.1 says it no longer needs checking here.
Vote is enabled only after the gates pass.
(A3; ADR-0050 §4; floor C3): who asserted it is
known, whether it is true is not (G10 item 57).
Alphabet Vote(grant), Vote(deny).
Under "all", any grant-seat deny or abstention is a denial; under unanimity every seat is a veto.
Voters are principals on every custody rung, because the anchor can evict them.
A person who operates and also votes holds two seats and is two principals (ADR-0037 §7, A4).

text.tspan: Veto seats · every cell Observer and every correlator in Build

svg.text: Alphabet Vote(deny) only: a seat whose alphabet lacks grant. Never an agent in the author's fault domain. A2.1 replaced
"the independent Observer replicated group (ADR-0008)".
A veto-seat deny is a denial; veto-seat silence is not. A "no finding" attestation would make semantic judgment an
enabling condition (ADR-0007).
Removed from the counted seats, and the ADR-0022 Vote envelope refuses its vote: no issuance can admit one.
ADR-0024 enabling condition with A2; every conjunct must hold
G = grantSeats \ {Author(a)}: recusal is a mechanism constant, not an issued value (§6)
|G| ≥ minGrant, else denied (R2)
quorum = "all": every counted grant seat granted (archetype, R1); otherwise |Granted| ≥ k with k ≥ 2 (R9)
A vote counts only as the triple ⟨grant, digest, evidence, rulesEpoch⟩; only recorded votes count
No veto seat has cast ⟨deny, digest, evidence, rulesEpoch⟩
A2.2 a veto seat with a Persona independent of the author's (ADR-0035 §5) was leased for the round, else stalls
A2.3 the author's cell Observer reported coverage to the seal of the author's round (ADR-0039 §3), else stalls
The veto check is any-of over the veto roster: one deny suffices, and adding veto seats never lowers safety
A rules change needs an anchor issuance plus a promotion (ADR-0026 §4): this quorum cannot change its own
One signed artifact crosses B1 into Run.
No strict subset of grant seats can promote (at "all").
A grant-seat deny or abstention; a veto-seat deny; recusal
leaves fewer seats than minGrant.
A timeout is never a grant: a mechanism constant (ex-R4).
No independent veto seat leased (A2.2), or no coverage to the
seal (A2.3): an absent Observer stalls promotion instead of
vetoing nothing.
Submit(digest)
Vote enabled
votes
roster at epoch e
quorum, minGrant
new epoch voids in-flight votes
A vote binds to (artifact digest, gate-evidence digest, rules epoch) (§3).
Any rules-epoch change voids in-flight votes: fencing, the same shape as leases. A vote on other evidence or an older epoch is not in Granted.
Vote(verdict, digest, evidence, rulesEpoch): seat held at rulesEpoch; grant only from a grant seat; terminal for the voter's round (ADR-0022
The authoritative vote is the admit decision in the consensus log (ADR-0015), retained as ADR-0028 F3.
A voter's round-topic emission carries the vote with a hash-and-pointer to its commentary in the ADR-0004 store; commentary is payload and erasable, the
vote is not.
So the round needs no effect-stream scheme: §7 does not rest on ADR-0021.
At the reference there is no promotion entry and no promote op: the admit that completes the tally is the event, and promoted_at in state is derived from
it. F3 retains the vote; what the archive says of the promotion is open (inventory finding 29).

text.tspan: What promotes, and what does not

svg.text: Promotion is a grant (§1): operational bundles, mechanism releases (including policy-floor and rules-floor changes) and Personas; since A3, seatings
(below), and a confinement profile, which the mechanism registers when the tally completes (ADR-0050 §4).
Runtime subtraction is not promotion (§9): e-stop, lease expiry, revocation and bundle(deny=all) need no quorum, are attributed, and are ordered
when they change replicated state. An operator's stop is a signed EndRound, Revoke or FenceEpoch (ADR-0050 §4).
Fast path for strictly subtractive bundles: deferred.

text.tspan: A promotion seats: the seating, the first lease, and who continues it (ADR-0024 A3; ADR-0050 §2)
Accepted · provisional · with ADR-0050 · bootstrap set

svg.text: "Promotion is a grant" taken literally (ToO §7.1). A principal's first lease is granted by the mechanism when a quorum completes, never by an operator; round by round, one operator continues what the quorum granted. So the quorum acts once per seating (ADR-0050 §2).
An artifact naming the principal, its seat, its Persona, its bundle revision, its confinement profile and
rung, its alphabet, and the labels a task for it may carry (A3; ADR-0050 §2).
Promoted like any other artifact, by the round above. An operator's Persona is promoted so, and an
operator is seated so.
Its schema, and whether it is one artifact or rides the Persona's and the bundle's promotions, is open
(ADR-0050 Open obligations).
PromotionEnabled as above: §2's quorum rule and §5's seat classes are unchanged by A3.
The gates were recorded by an operator's signed AttestGates.
A2.2 and A2.3 still apply: a veto seat independent of the author leased for the round, and coverage to the
seal, or the round stalls.
A confinement profile promoted the same way is registered by the mechanism when the tally completes; it
is no longer an operator's request (ADR-0050 §4).

text.tspan: 3 · The mechanism grants the first lease

svg.text: At a fresh fence, with no request from anyone (ADR-0050 §2).
First leases are not actions and have no floor entry: the mechanism grants one when a quorum completes
The seating carries the round's task, by digest with its label on the log; the label must be one the seating
allows (ADR-0050 §5).
Successor grant (Regrant): the next round, every field the last lease's or narrower, only round advancing.
Renewal (Renew) keeps the round (ADR-0031 §4).
Needs a live lease and a live peer in the domain (C1, C2, C5); never itself (C6); the task's label in the
seating's bounds (C8).
Monotone: it can keep a quorum's grant going and narrow it, and cannot widen it.
Anything wider is a first lease: a different Persona, bundle, profile or seat, or a new variant in the alphabet needs a new seating and a quorum (ADR-0050 §2)

text.tspan: Who grants a first lease (ADR-0050 §2, the record's table)
A seat on a roster the rules name (grant, veto, anchor) at

svg.text: An anchor issuance (ADR-0025; ADR-0029 §5)
Something must be seated before anything can be promoted
A promotion (ADR-0024)
"Promotion is a grant"
An emergency seating is one of these too: prepared by promotion, and activated for one round by the break-glass roster's quorum and not by a tally; an operator's Regrant or Renew
naming an emergency seat is refused (ADR-0050 §2 R6; ADR-0052 §2). Drawn in D5.
The ceremony's first step seats the first operators by issuance, at least three in each
domain at the archetype, each with a Persona and a key, with the identity providers' keys
in the issued rules (ADR-0029 A3; ADR-0025 A3 (a), (f)).

text.tspan: Until an operator is seated nothing can be regranted, and a promotion needs Build

svg.text: Whether a bootstrap module is owed for the genesis seating is not decided (ADR-0029

text.tspan: At the reference: a BOOTSTRAP socket seats
Not built · first lease from a quorum
A promoted seating that grants a first lease, and the first operators seated by an

svg.text: anchor issuance, are not built (ADR-0050 §10, R10; G10 §1.2, §8).
The unsigned operator socket is kept as a marked BOOTSTRAP path that seats and
does nothing else: whoever reaches it can seat (D-0050-1 for that one step; I47 (a)).
It refuses a grant that keeps a seat's seated binding while two operators of its domain are
live: that is a successor, and theirs to make (not_a_first_seating).
Every successor grant, renewal, gate attestation and stop is a signed request decided by
C1 to C9 (ADR-0050 R9).
ADR-0050 stops being provisional when its debts are met and the custodian records it:
a first lease from a completed tally, with a promoted seating; the first operators seated by
an anchor issuance; a Regrant at rung 1 or above, which has to launch a guest; an
operator's Persona record and lineage; and a review by a reader who is not the drafter
Until then, A3 is subject to redesign with it, and anything citing it says "author-ratified,
provisional" (ADR-0029 A4).

text.tspan: Quorum: archetype "all" versus a threshold k, and the two declared degeneracies

svg.text: Every counted grant seat must grant; a grant-seat deny or abstention denies.
Required by R1
A grant-vote threshold over the counted seats: D-0024-1, k-of-n
Relaxes R1; R9 keeps k ≥ 2
One signer: D-0024-2, the pre-0024 status quo
Relaxes R1, R9 and R2
Withdrawn (rev 5): it is k = 1 and tolerates no Byzantine approver, never the
k-of-n degeneracy it appeared to be
A threshold means something only with at least three counted seats: at two, k ≥ 2 is unanimity (ADR-0026 §7 finding 3).
k-of-n grant seats
No promotion without every grant seat
Tolerance of n−k Byzantine approvers
Liveness under n−k absent approvers
Single signer (the pre-0024 status
quo)
Grants need consensus
All approver fault tolerance; reintroduces a privileged human grant
Throughput

Both ratified with ADR-0024 as declarations (B2). Each is a change to issued quorum and minGrant, so it relaxes ADR-0026 entries, not this record, and needs an anchor issuance plus a promotion under the rule being replaced. A promotion degeneracy is a mechanism release;
approver fault tolerance and anchor recoverability are declared independently (ToO §7.7).

text.tspan: Stated costs, and where the record stands

svg.text: Liveness equals the availability of every grant seat, Persona and incident-driven bundle promotions included.
Liveness assumption: weak fairness on Vote for grant seats, an assumption about people.
A2 adds a second: weak fairness on an independent Observer's lease and its coverage, an assumption about a
deployment.
Correlated review failure is untouched: unanimous humans reading the same vacuous gate output fail together
(Knight & Leveson).
Floor fitness, a fourth gate (NIST MEASURE 2.13), now has an owner and a time, the bootstrap reviewer at
bootstrap (ADR-0029 A4; ADR-0030 A3), and no test (G10 items 2, 87).
One compromised seat is a veto until the anchor reissues the roster.
Voters are Mediated: promotion gains attribution and authorization, not safety properties.

text.tspan: Accepted · bootstrap set · A2 in force · A3 provisional

svg.text: ADR-0024 is Accepted (genesis), 2026.09.23, at revision 5, in Batch 2.
No confirmation marker: a bootstrap record (ADR-0029 §4); confirmation runs under it. ADR-0029 A2's
full-corpus review reaches it before bootstrap: a reader, not a confirmation promotion.
A2 ratified 2026.09.29 (Batch 15), in genesis for the same reason.
A3 ratified 2026.10.05 (Batch 34), provisional with ADR-0050: in force and subject to redesign. In the bootstrap
set, so not confirmation-required; the genesis attestation must name it as provisional (ADR-0029 A4). Not
reviewed by a reader other than the drafter.
In the reference: A2.1 (veto roster kinds) and A2.3 (Tally::Stalled until coverage) are in force; A2.2 is not
(G18): no independence table exists, since ADR-0035 is Proposed and §4 is unbuilt.
A3 is not built: no promoted seating grants a first lease; the BOOTSTRAP socket seats (below; I47).
Owed: the ADR-0026 §6 non-vacuity rerun with A2.2 and A2.3 as conjuncts (G10 §2.1); the Promotion bootstrap
module (StaleVotesNeverCount), not drafted, which also owes a model of deciding before committing (ToO §9);
independent evidence and seat diversity, candidate floor entries.
